motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing Item 12.E. from the agenda, and moving Items 11.B., 12.A, and 12.C. to the scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Routine consent items approved in one vote
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, dropping one item from the agenda entirely and pulling three others out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: This is procedural — a single vote covering routine items. Nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Approve the Eagle Square Commercial Preliminary Plat with the following condition: Eagle Mounta…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Eagle Square Commercial Preliminary Plat with the following condition: Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 17, 2024 Page 5 of 15 1. The traffic study be utilized to locate the entrance off of Pony Express Parkway into the south portion of the commercial development, recognizing it is located on the southeast portion of the preliminary plat and aligns with intersection to the south. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Eagle Square shopping center layout approved
motions.summary: The city approved the preliminary layout for the Eagle Square commercial development, requiring a traffic study to determine where its Pony Express Parkway entrance goes.
motions.impact: A commercial development moves ahead off Pony Express Parkway. The condition requires the south entrance to line up with the intersection across the road, based on the traffic study.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Six Wayfinding Signs.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Six Wayfinding Signs with Impact Signs. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Six new wayfinding signs
motions.summary: The council took up an agreement with Impact Signs to supply six wayfinding signs for the city.
motions.impact: If it goes ahead, six signs directing people around the city get installed. The motion does not say where they go or what they cost.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Affordable Housing Plan. Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 17, 2024 Page 6 of 15
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Affordable Housing Plan, to be brought to a future meeting with the changes the Council discussed. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Affordable housing plan put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the city's affordable housing plan, sending it back with changes to be brought to a future meeting.
motions.impact: No affordable housing policy takes effect yet. If you have been following this plan, it returns to the council after revisions.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 17, 2024 Page 7 of 15 within The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties Master Development Areas with the following designations: Property Number Land Use Designation EMP 29 Community Commercial EMP 30 Community Commercial EMP 31 Community Commercial 1 Community Commercial 2 Community Commercial 3 Community Commercial 4 Community Commercial 5 Community Commercial 6 Community Commercial 7 Community Commercial 8 Community Commercial 9 Parks and Open Space 10 Parks and Open Space 11 Foothill Residential 12 Community Commercial 13 Parks and Open Space 14 Parks and Open Space Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Long-range map redrawn for the same 17 parcels
motions.summary: The city updated its long-range land use map for the same 17 properties: community commercial on twelve, parks and open space on four, foothill residential on one.
motions.impact: The land use map is the city's long-term plan for what goes where. This keeps it consistent with the zoning change, and you will see nothing different on the ground today.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands within The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties Master Development Areas with the following designations: Property Number Zone EMP 29 CN EMP 30 CN EMP 31 CN 1 CN 2 CN 3 CN 4 CN 5 CN 6 CN 7 CN 8 CN 9 AG 10 AG 11 Foothill Residential 12 CN 13 OSN 14 OSN Councilmember Clark seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands within The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties Master Development Areas with the following designations: Property Number Zone EMP 29 CN EMP 30 CN EMP 31 CN 1 CN 2 CN 3 CN 4 CN 5 CN 6 CN 7 CN 8 CN 9 AG 10 AG 11 Foothill Residential 12 CN 13 OSN 14 OSN Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 17 parcels rezoned near The Ranches
motions.summary: The city rezoned 17 properties in The Ranches and Eagle Mountain Properties areas: twelve for neighborhood commercial, two agricultural, two open space, one foothill residential.
motions.impact: This clears the way for shops and businesses on most of these parcels instead of homes, and sets two areas aside as open space. Nothing is built yet — zoning only sets what is allowed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Second Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Second Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mid-year change to this year's city budget
motions.summary: The city approved a second round of changes to its 2024-2025 budget; the motion itself does not say what was moved or added.
motions.impact: A budget amendment shifts money between city accounts partway through the year. The motion gives no detail on the specific spending, so there is nothing here for you to act on.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Rose Ranch from Agriculture to the R2 and R3 Zones with the following conditions: 1. Add tabletop crosswalks on the Pony Express Trail and a historical marker; and Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 17, 2024 Page 10 of 15 2. Complete the Pony Express Trail as a finished space
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Rose Ranch from Agriculture to the R2 and R3 Zones with the following conditions: 1. Add tabletop crosswalks on the Pony Express Trail and a historical marker; and Eagle Mountain City Council Meeting – September 17, 2024 Page 10 of 15 2. Complete the Pony Express Trail as a finished space. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch: farmland to housing zones
motions.summary: The council took up a plan to rezone the Rose Ranch land from farmland to the R2 and R3 housing zones, with conditions attached.
motions.impact: If it goes ahead, this land shifts from farmland to housing. The conditions require raised crosswalks on the Pony Express Trail, a historical marker, and the trail finished as usable space.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 Diagrams Relating to Rights-of-Way Profiles with direction to staff to return with recommendations on the Rural 50-foot right-of-way for curb and gutter and an additional sidewalk
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 Diagrams Relating to Rights-of-Way Profiles with direction to staff to return with recommendations on the Rural 50-foot right-of-way for curb and gutter and an additional sidewalk. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Street width rules held for a second look
motions.summary: The council delayed changes to the city's right-of-way diagrams, asking staff to return with recommendations on curb, gutter and a sidewalk for rural 50-foot roads.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet. These diagrams set how wide new streets are and whether they get sidewalks, so this mainly affects future subdivisions, not streets you already drive.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.10 Definitions and 17.25 Residential Zones
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.10 Definitions and 17.25 Residential Zones. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council rejects changes to residential zone rules
motions.summary: The council turned down proposed changes to the definitions and residential zoning chapters of the city code.
motions.impact: Nothing changes — the rules for residential zones stay exactly as they were.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise, to allow staff to make changes and bring the item back to the next City Council meeting. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise and nuisance rules sent back to staff
motions.summary: The council delayed changes to the city's nuisance and noise rules, asking staff to revise them and bring them back at the next meeting.
motions.impact: The current noise and nuisance rules stay in force for now. Any change to how the city handles complaints has to wait for a revised version.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 12.35 Public Art.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 12.35 Public Art. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update the city's public art rules
motions.summary: The city changed the public art chapter of its municipal code; the motion does not say what the changes were.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. These rules govern how the city itself handles public art, not anything a resident has to do.

motions.item_title: Set “A review of Conditional Uses in Zoning Code leading to reclassification based on defined s…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to set “A review of Conditional Uses in Zoning Code leading to reclassification based on defined specifications” as “Done” on the Legislative Priorities List, and remove “Neighborhood Residential 1 Lot Size Distribution” from the Legislative Priorities List as it has been tabled by the City Council. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council cleans up its own priorities list
motions.summary: The council marked its review of conditional uses in the zoning code as finished and dropped a tabled item on lot sizes from its priorities list.
motions.impact: This is housekeeping about the council's own to-do list — nothing changes for residents.
